author: .just_kk
content:
<@&595681771690000403> hello! Responding to the commend in ACDC zoom chat.

We discussed this EIP a lot on the p2p breakouts and similar ideas were discussed for years.  We can justify any design decisions if you think this EIP is still not mature enough.

Glamsterdam increases the gas limit and Hegota potentially decreases slot time. Also we need to make room for additional traffic that PQ will bring + similar machinery will be used for proofs propagation.

The scope is minimal and does not require any networking stack changes. Most of the EIP is just chunking the message + introducing one field in the bid.

Happy to reiterate on any detail if you had any particular concerns. Or if you need some additional data to be convinced of necessity of the EIP let us know

author: matthewkeil
content:
ill be honest, im not a big fan of the feature. it feels like a premature optimization.

i also dont really agree that its a minimal change. there is no "partial" gossip anything that is "minimal".  the switch from blobs to columns was a massive lift.  and from columns to cell-DAS was as well

i think when we see mainnet data on how payloads actually propagate i will be easier to convince though

author: .just_kk
content:
Some gossip data
https://investigations.ethpandaops.io/2026-05/block-size-vs-propagation/

So around ~800-900ms for ~200KB blocks. In the past there were blocks of size ~1MB.
Glamsterdam increases the limits and adds the BALs so payloads will get larger. We could easily expect 300-500KB blocks. 
With EIP-7870 nodes (which is the worst case assumption) in our simulations it takes ~4 seconds to reach 95% of nodes.

The main change is splitting the serialized envelope into 64 chunks and just sending them into the topic. It is nowhere near to the PeerDAS complexity

author: .just_kk
content: We're so much inefficient today by downloading the full payload before we forward it further. We're getting 3-4x latency decrease if we send individual chunks and can start forwarding them before we received the full message
